Author: Subhash Chandra Sharma
Bench: Subhash Chandra Sharma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 82
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 933 of 2023
Applicant :- Shameen

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.And Another Counsel for Applicant :- Kamlesh Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Kamla Dinkar Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Mrs. Kamla Dinkar, learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.

This anticipatory bail application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 474 of 2022, under sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 504, 506 I.P.C., Police Station Gajraula, District Amroha.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that in this case applicant has falsely been implicated.

Further it is submitted that the residential land measuring 496.28 square meter was purchased by the applicant Shameen through registered sale deed in the year 2014 and then it was sold by him in favour of the present informant through registered sale deed dated 05.03.2022 even though the applicant got mutation done in his name ex-parte which was set aside after objection made by the informant.
Later on the applicant sold the land relating to other Gata numbers in favour of several purchasers but he did not sell the land belonging to the informant.

It is also Shameen vs State Of U.P.And Another on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117866040/
1 submitted that a civil suit was also filed by the informant against the applicant which is still pending.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The dispute is of purely civil nature therefore no criminal offence is made out against the applicant.
Lastly, it is submitted that applicant is under apprehension of imminent arrest.

In case,
the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation, so requested for anticipatory bail.

Learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid and urged that in this case the applicant himself fraudulently sold the land in favour of other persons which was already sold by him in favour of the informant and he also got the mutation done in his name which was set aside on objection made by the informant. Since applicant had executed several sale deeds in relation to the same property it shows his mala fides therefore he cannot be said to be entitled for anticipatory bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for both the parties as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of record, there appears no ground to grant anticipatory bail in favour of the applicant.
Accordingly, this anticipatory bail application is rejected.

However, as per submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant, in case, he appears and moves bail application before the learned Court concerned, it shall be heard and disposed of as expeditiously as possible in accordance with law.

Order Date :- 23.3.2023 Suraj Srivastav  Shameen vs State Of U.P.And Another on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117866040/
